title: Onboard Velocity: 90-Day Sprint Plan for New Enterprise Customers
summary: A sprint-oriented 90-day onboarding and adoption playbook designed for enterprise accounts that need predictable time-to-value and clear renewal signaling. Emphasizes short feedback loops, integration milestones, and a compact renewal tracker for early risk detection.
objectives: Deliver first production inference flow within 30 days
Achieve product-level adoption metric (25% active usage of targeted routes) by day 60
Reach baseline business KPIs tied to customer use-case (latency < target, cost per 1k tokens within agreed threshold) by day 90
Establish renewal readiness with a formal health score and executive alignment before day 75
success_metrics: Percent of key routes instrumented and monitored (goal: 100% by day 30)
Adoption: % of seats or apps using Redwood API weekly (goal: 25% by day 60)
Quality: share of responses within acceptable eval thresholds (goal: > 90%)
Renewal health score (see formula below) — green if >= 85
sprint_plan: Sprint 0 — Pre-kickoff (-7 to 0): - Confirm contract / access and security checklist; - Share kickoff agenda and stub integration guide; - Provision sandbox creds and baseline telemetry (dataplane + cost metrics).

Sprint 1 — Week 1 (Day 1-7): Kickoff & rapid discovery - Kickoff with exec sponsor + technical lead; - Align success metrics and SLAs; - Run smoke tests using sample payloads; - Deliver 'first request' playbook and confirm SDK access. Deliverable: smoke-test report + action items.

Sprint 2 — Weeks 2-4 (Day 8-30): Integration & core flows - Technical onboarding: embed API calls into dev flow; - Set up tracing and route-level dashboards; - Run 3 canonical prompts/flows and capture baselines; - Hold weekly triage with engineering. Deliverable: 'integration milestones' sign-off (see CSV template).

Sprint 3 — Weeks 5-8 (Day 31-60): Expansion & adoption - Optimize batching/caching as suggested by Redwood Optimize; - Run internal training for product and support teams; - Launch internal pilot with a subset of users; - Track adoption KPIs and iterate prompts/config. Deliverable: adoption runbook + KPI dashboard.

Sprint 4 — Weeks 9-13 (Day 61-90): Stabilize & prepare renewal - Harden SLOs, finalize runbooks, and prepare exec summary; - Conduct joint business review (pre-QBR) and surface renewal recommendation; - Create a hands-off operating cadence for ongoing ops. Deliverable: renewal readiness packet + health score.

renewal_tracker_template:
Columns: account,ARR,contract_end,health_score,last_exec_touch,top_risks,renewal_probability,input_owner
Instructions: update weekly; color code risks (red/yellow/green); tie probability to health score bands (>=85: high, 70-84: medium, <70: low)
risk_mitigation: If latency or error spikes during pilot: enable Canary routing to a lower-utilization region and escalate to infra on-call
If cost projections exceed agreed threshold: apply suggested quantization profile and partner with Redwood Optimize team for batching recommendations
If adoption stalls: run a 2-week focused prompt workshop with product owners and provide sample prompts and template tests
raci_quick_reference: R: Customer Eng, A: CS Lead, C: Solutions Eng + Product, I: Exec Sponsor — Use for milestone sign-offs and extension approvals
sample_emails: Kickoff invite (subject): Redwood kickoff — <Account Name> / Next steps; Body: Hi team — thanks for partnering. Agenda: 1) exec goals 2) technical scope 3) timelines 4) success metrics. Please attach admin contact and required IP allowlists.

Day-30 check-in (subject): 30-day integration update — action items; Body: Hi — progress looks good. Attached: smoke-test & integration sign-off. Three blockers identified: X, Y, Z. Proposed owners and deadlines included.
qbr_preparation_checklist: - Pull health score and underlying metrics (usage, errors, latency) - Collect top 3 wins and top 3 risks - Update renewal tracker and probability - Prepare 1-page exec summary with ask (extend/expand/close) - Schedule 30-minute executive review the week before contract milestone
escalation_path: 1) CS Lead -> 2) Solutions Eng Manager -> 3) Platform Eng Director -> 4) Customer Exec Sponsor. Use pager for Sev1 issues and tag #cust-incident in Slack.
